new_findings.text: This packet publishes TWO incompatible frame-to-stage vertical transforms for video B and both are marked HELD. Model A (ui-hud/frame-to-stage-mapping-is-anisotropic, ui-hud/slot-strip-matches-all-three-constants): offsetY = 0, vertical scale 1080/480 = 2.250, horizontal 2.270, the 0.9% difference blamed on a re-encode stretch. Model B (ui-hud/frame-to-stage-transform, ui-hud/slot-box-measurement-corrected): a single uniform scale ~2.269 with origin (52, -5.0), i.e. ~5 px cropped off the top and bottom because 480 x 2.269 = 1089 > 1080. On my own measurement of the cited frame, Model B is the better-supported one and Model A should not be adopted as the lane convention. Evidence: (1) the pillarbox is exactly 52 px of black on BOTH sides, so content = 1816 px = 800 x 2.270 - a genuine 2.250 fit would leave 60 px pillarboxes, which the frame does not show; (2) under Model B the empty slot box is exactly 48 x 48 game px centred at exactly game (640, 450), matching BattleUI.as:133-134 to the integer, while under Model A it is 48.4 x 48.0 (non-square) centred at 451.8; (3) the frame box measures square (112 x 112 at threshold 150), which an anisotropic mapping would not produce. Model A is not disproved - the ~1 px thresholds leave room - but it carries an unreconciled 1.8 game-px residual against a code-known constant and Model B carries 0.2.

Of the sixteen findWeight() > getCarryingWeight() guards in the Android build, only eight carry the !GameEngine.isPvPRoomMode() prefix. Among the eight sites cited by string-table/weight-gate-is-a-travel-guard-in-code, five have the exemption (Obj_TownSign:44, Obj_DirectionSign:159, Obj_PathBush:110, Obj_HiddenTemple:187, Obj_DragonDancePath:275) and three do NOT (Obj_Hut:70, NodeUI:379, InteractUI:1730).
